# agent-browser

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP with accessibility-tree snapshots and compact `@eN` element refs.

Install: `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`

## Start here

This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide. Before running any `agent-browser` command, load the actual workflow content from the CLI:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core             # start here — workflows, common patterns, troubleshooting
agent-browser skills get core --full      # include full command reference and templates
```

The CLI serves skill content that always matches the installed version, so instructions never go stale. The content in this stub cannot change between releases, which is why it just points at `skills get core`.

## Specialized skills

Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser web pages:

```bash
agent-browser skills get electron          # Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, ...)
agent-browser skills get slack             # Slack workspace automation
agent-browser skills get dogfood           # Exploratory testing / QA / bug hunts
agent-browser skills get derive-client     # Record a HAR, derive a standalone API client for a site
agent-browser skills get vercel-sandbox    # agent-browser inside Vercel Sandbox microVMs
agent-browser skills get agentcore         # AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers
```

Run `agent-browser skills list` to see everything available on the installed version.

## Why agent-browser

- Fast native Rust CLI, not a Node.js wrapper
- Works with any AI agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Continue, Windsurf, etc.)
- Chrome/Chromium via CDP with no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency
- Accessibility-tree snapshots with element refs for reliable interaction
- Sessions, authentication vault, state persistence, video recording
- Specialized skills for Electron apps, Slack, exploratory testing, cloud providers

## Observability Dashboard

The dashboard runs independently of browser sessions on port 4848 and can also be opened through a proxied or forwarded URL such as `https://dashboard.agent-browser.localhost`. Agents should stay on the dashboard origin: session tabs, status, and stream traffic are proxied internally, so session ports do not need to be exposed.

# agent-browser core

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact `@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of parsing raw HTML.

Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).

## The core loop

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
```

Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become **stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your next ref interaction.

## Always use your own session

Before your first command, set a named session for the whole task:

```bash
export AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION="$(agent-browser session id --scope worktree --prefix task)"
```

The default (unnamed) session is a single shared browser: it is shared with every other agent on the machine and it persists across conversations, so working in it can hijack another agent's page mid-task or navigate away from something the human left open. Every example below assumes a named session is active. See [Run multiple browsers in parallel](#run-multiple-browsers-in-parallel) and `references/session-management.md`.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Install once
npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install

# Linux hosts can install required browser libraries too
agent-browser install --with-deps

# Take a screenshot of a page
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser screenshot home.png
agent-browser close

# Search, click a result, and capture it
agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
agent-browser press Enter
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
agent-browser screenshot result.png
```

The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single session. By default, an inactive daemon saves configured restore state, closes its headless browser, and exits after one hour; the next command starts it again. Without `--restore` or another restore key, shutdown discards transient browser state and open tabs. Dashboard mouse, keyboard, and touch input count as activity. Headed browsers, Safari and iOS WebDriver sessions, and user-attached browsers are exempt from the default; provider-owned cloud browsers are not. Use `--idle-timeout <time>` or `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` to tune the timeout, and use `0` to disable it. Still run `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.

## MCP integration

For tools that support Model Context Protocol servers, start the stdio server:

```bash
agent-browser mcp
agent-browser mcp --tools all
agent-browser mcp --tools core,network,react
```

Configure the MCP client to launch `agent-browser` with `["mcp"]`. The server defaults to MCP protocol 2025-11-25 and accepts older supported client protocol versions during initialization. The default tools profile is `core`, which keeps MCP context small for everyday browser automation. Use `--tools all` for the full typed CLI parity surface, or combine profiles with commas, such as `--tools core,network,react`. Profiles are `core`, `network`, `state`, `debug`, `tabs`, `react`, `mobile`, and `all`; the `debug` profile includes accessibility audits, plugin registry, and command.run tools. Each tool accepts typed arguments plus `extraArgs` for advanced CLI flags and exact CLI parity. The common `allowedDomains` array maps to `--allowed-domains` and activates the same WebRTC containment and launch-mode restrictions, while `idleTimeout` maps to `--idle-timeout`. Tool discovery is paginated and includes read-only/open-world annotations so modern MCP clients can load the large typed surface incrementally. Use the tool `session` argument or `AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION` to isolate browser sessions.

## eve agent integration

For eve agents, mount the `@agent-browser/eve` extension instead of hand-writing browser tools. It adds namespaced tools such as `browser__navigate`, `browser__snapshot`, `browser__click`, `browser__fill`, `browser__find`, and `browser__screenshot`, all backed by agent-browser running inside the eve sandbox. The sandbox bootstrap helpers (`installAgentBrowser`, `agentBrowserRevalidationKey`) ship with the same package under `@agent-browser/eve/sandbox`, so `agent/sandbox.ts` needs no extra dependency.

## Reading a page

```bash
agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser read                         # read rendered active-tab DOM
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide  # docs-friendly fetch, prefers markdown
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide --filter auth  # one matching section
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com/guide --outline  # compact page headings
agent-browser read https://docs.example.com --llms index --filter auth  # compact llms.txt discovery
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

Use `read [url]` when you need to consume documentation or other text pages rather than interact with a rendered UI. Omit the URL to read the rendered DOM of the active tab in the current browser session, including browser auth state and client-side updates. Explicit URL reads send `Accept: text/markdown`, try the same URL with `.md` appended when the first response is not markdown, walk ancestor paths toward `/` to find the nearest `llms.txt` for a matching docs link, print markdown/plain text when available, and fall back to readable text extracted from HTML without launching Chrome. Add `--filter <text>` to narrow a page to matching heading sections, `--outline` for compact headings on one page, `--llms index` for a compact nearest-ancestor `llms.txt` link list, and `--llms full` only when you explicitly need `llms-full.txt`. With `--llms` or `--require-md`, omitting the URL uses the active tab URL because those modes depend on HTTP resources. With `--llms` or `--outline`, `--filter <text>` narrows links, sections, or headings. Add `--require-md` when you specifically want to verify markdown negotiation, `--raw` when you need the response body unchanged, and `--json` when you need metadata such as `source` and `contentType`. Global safeguards such as `--allowed-domains`, `--content-boundaries`, and `--max-output` also apply to read fetches and output.

For sessions that handle sensitive data, use `--allowed-domains` to restrict navigations and page-initiated network traffic. Supported Chromium sessions also disable `RTCPeerConnection` while the allowlist is active so WebRTC STUN, TURN, and related DNS traffic cannot bypass the HTTP filter. Dedicated and shared workers are guarded with a bootstrap wrapper; if a page CSP forbids that wrapper, the worker fails closed rather than running without the allowlist guard. Pre-existing CDP sessions, auto-connect, Chrome profiles, direct-page provider plugins, agent-browser restore or state-file replay, raw Chrome args that select profiles, restore sessions, or open startup pages, iOS, and Safari reject this option because agent-browser cannot install equivalent containment before page scripts run. This is browser-level containment, not an operating-system firewall; see [Trust boundaries](references/trust-boundaries.md) for deployment guidance.

## Interacting

```bash
agent-browser click @e1                   # click
agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
```

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief > **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers, > gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.** ## 1. The story You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker: centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals, motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix its quality. You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their topics and attach documents. Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data - orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.) ## 2. The task Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your **buyer agent** 1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package; 2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like; 3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away. **How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship as people do; padding does not buy price. **Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") - or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still move on other terms. ## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00) | What | Where | |---|---| | This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` | | **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` | | **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) | | **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes | You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT. **Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail, and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once** on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it. Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive). **Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use, practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00. **`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real suppliers act is part of the challenge. **The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them - improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts. ## 4. The data The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts, invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM); framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30). - **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `:[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`. - What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional. - **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it. ## 5. How a negotiation works - **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF. - **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments. - **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status - `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out; and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60 seconds. - **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3 suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case. - **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after the last round, end the thread. - **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF. **Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal. **What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says `verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or `duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business. **What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person. ## 6. The score: total cost in € Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your **fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its **category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill. | Part of C | How | |---|---| | Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price | | Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it | | Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need | | Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk | | The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) | **Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none); some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C. **Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%, reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net. | | Terms | C | |---|---|---| | C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 | | Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 | | C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 | | **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** | The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say €46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0. ## 7. Rules 1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard` and their JSON). 2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations. 3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal. 4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys. 5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data. ## 8. The weekend | When | What | |---|---| | Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live | | Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 | | Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend | | Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) | | Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) | | Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup | | Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves | | Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) | | Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced | | Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) | | Sun 16:30 | Awards | **The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once, each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed. The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows** - no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite the Sunday release. ## 9. Selection and prizes - **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00: 5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury. - **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning: weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach, explainability, craft)⟧. - **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone. - **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10 cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30. ## 10. Tips - **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording. - **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what it is dealing with - and what will move it. - **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms. - **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values. - **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer. - **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes. # Submission and pitch What to hand in for the Tacto track, and how the pitch works. Deadline: **Sunday 12:00 on ehl.gg**. ## What to submit 1. **Your repo:** the agent and a README that says how to run it (setup, the environment variables it needs, without values, and the command). Put the **commit hash** your agent runs in the final into the description. The jury and tum.ai must be able to open the repo; tum.ai runs a code agent over every submission. 2. **A short description** of your approach: how your agent prepares, what it reads in the data, how it decides what to offer, and when it closes or walks away. 3. **Slides** for the pitch. The top 10 present them from 13:00. Keep every key out of the repo: no `.env`, no LLM key, no arena key. ## At 12:00 your agent is already running The code freeze and the Live Final start together, so start your agent before 12:00 and leave it running: ```bash uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10 ``` Or your own runner that polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`. The kit's runner waits for wave 1, plays each wave's cases in parallel within the 8-minute cap and stops after the fifth wave. From 12:00 there is no human in the loop, and your agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard` or `/results`. We check the top 10 for pushes after the freeze. Checklist for 11:30: - The machine and network you use for the final; one practice case went through it at the 09:00 pre-flight. - `uv run arena data` ran after 08:00, so the Sunday release sits next to the package. - `uv run arena me` answers with your team: the key works. - LLM credits and rate limits for about an hour of parallel play. - The runner is started and logs to a file; the laptop is on power and does not sleep. ## The pitch - **The top 10:** the ten teams with the most points after the five waves. - **5 minutes pitch + 2 minutes of questions**, from 13:00. tum.ai keeps the time; the slot does not stretch. - **Every replay is open to the jury.** After the final, each case on https://arena.tacto.ai/results links to its replay. Pick one negotiation and walk us through it. - Questions to expect: Why did your agent write that? Would it have worked on a real supplier? What did your agent learn about suppliers, and from where? - ⟦Q2: how the Live Final score and the jury combine for places 1-3, and the jury criteria⟧ # Supplier scorecard - method Each row (`sc:@`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to the supplier, so both sides know it. - **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date. Partial deliveries count as separate lines. - **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN). - **open_8d_overdue**: supplier-caused complaints older than 60 days without a closed 8D report at quarter end. - **score** = 0.5 x otd_pct + 0.5 x quality points - 5 x open_8d_overdue, with quality points = 100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000). - **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.

# Can your agent win a tender?

Build an AI agent that works through the software a sales engineer uses every day: a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox. It clicks through them like a person would, collects the facts and submits a priced bid. Every submission runs in a sandbox and lands on a live leaderboard. At the end, the winners are picked on performance on data nobody has seen first, then on the public leaderboard, then on the elegance of the system.

## From RFQ to bid

Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid.

The challenge →

-

01 · tender-portalOpen site ↗

### Tender portalVergabeportal

The public tender, its bill of quantities, the bidder Q&A that changes quantities, and the bid configurator.

Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes and ZIP files, a deadline in another timezone.

-

02 · customer-portalOpen site ↗

### Supplier portalLieferantenportal

The buyer's technical specification and its revisions.

Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables.

-

03 · erpOpen site ↗

### ERP

Your company's materials, stock, lead times and price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales.

SAP-style transaction codes, an F4 search popup, status codes, a short session timeout.

-

04 · mailOpen site ↗

### WebmailWerkpost

Your sales inbox, with the sales director's discount approval and the signing TAN.

Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, an archive folder, paging.

Test runs, scouting and the leaderboard all use these websites with public data. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. Scout them yourself →

## How it works

Getting started →

- 01

### Form a team

Sign in with GitHub, create a team and invite your teammates. Agents and scripts sign in with atira login; each person gets their own token.

- 02

### Develop locally

Look around the websites, fork the starter kit and run your agent from your laptop with atira scout --env. These runs aren't scored.

- 03

### Test in the sandbox

Upload your package as a test run. Watch its browser live, read its logs, replay its recording.

- 04

### Submit

Each submission is checked automatically, then runs once in the sandbox. Its score sets your place on the leaderboard.

Rules at a glance: Fair play

## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, atira models proxy gives you a URL and key (setup on your team page). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

How to call them →

-

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

LimitsNo usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: choice picks one of your options, noul gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and score rates on a scale you set. See Cloudflare's announcement and the benchmarks. Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

# From RFQ to bid

Turn a public tender into a correct, signed bid without a person touching it.

You work for a German hydraulics manufacturer that wants to bid on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. What you need is spread over four websites: the tender portal, a supplier portal with the buyer's specification, your company's ERP and the sales inbox. They behave like real business software, with logins, popups, session timeouts and outdated documents. Your agent reads all of it, applies the bid rules and enters one priced, signed bid in the tender portal.

## Public and private data

There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

Public dataset

The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.

Private dataset

When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.

## The rules

The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.

- 01 · Quantity

The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.

- 02 · Requirement

The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.

- 03 · Material

The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.

- 04 · Unit price

The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.

- 05 · Discount

The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.

- 06 · Lead time

The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.

- 07 · Total

The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.

- 08 · Decision

Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.

- 09 · Partial submission

Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.

- 10 · Finding records

The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.

- 11 · Agent requirement

A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.

- 12 · Commercial clauses

A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.

- 13 · Withdrawn answers

A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.

- 14 · Scoped amendments

After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.

- 15 · Shared stock

Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.

- 16 · Conditional discount

The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.

- 17 · Units

Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.

- 18 · Pricing breakdown

Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.

- 19

These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.

- 20 · Technical derivation

For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.

- 21 · Authority and time

Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.

- 22 · Currency

The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.

- 23 · Packaging

Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.

- 24 · Delivery

Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.

- 25 · Shared setup

Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.

- 26 · Project bonus

The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.

- 27 · Final price

Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.

- 28 · Metal indices

Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.

- 29 · Scoring in bid cases

Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (atira scout --env), then test in the sandbox: atira test-run uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on your team page. A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, $ATIRA_TOKEN holds your personal token (sign in with atira login, then atira token).

The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.

- 02

### Read

Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.

- 03

### Work the websites

It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.

- 04

### Submit

It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.

- 05

### Scored

The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.

Private dataset

It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.
## The rules
The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.
- 01 · Quantity
The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
- 02 · Requirement
The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
- 03 · Material
The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
- 04 · Unit price
The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
- 05 · Discount
The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
- 06 · Lead time
The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
- 07 · Total
The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
- 08 · Decision
Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
- 09 · Partial submission
Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- 10 · Finding records
The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- 11 · Agent requirement
A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- 12 · Commercial clauses
A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- 13 · Withdrawn answers
A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- 14 · Scoped amendments
After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- 15 · Shared stock
Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- 16 · Conditional discount
The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
- 17 · Units
Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
- 18 · Pricing breakdown
Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
- 19
These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
- 20 · Technical derivation
For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
- 21 · Authority and time
Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
- 22 · Currency
The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
- 23 · Packaging
Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
- 24 · Delivery
Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
- 25 · Shared setup
Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
- 26 · Project bonus
The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
- 27 · Final price
Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
- 28 · Metal indices
Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
- 29 · Scoring in bid cases
Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

# Fair play
**Rules at a glance**
You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.
**Not allowed**
- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.
**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.
The details follow.
## Allowed
- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.
## Not allowed
- Hardcoding values copied from the public scenario or its websites into code, config, prompts or notes, including defaults and fallbacks: tender references, material numbers, prices, totals, discounts, logins and TANs. Facts the task brief states for every scenario, such as the sales director's mailbox, are
  rules you may use.
- A scripted solution. Your agent system must be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the
  information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a
  page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for), and several agents and browsers may work
  in parallel. Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback,
  and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
- Bundling or running a local model, or reaching any model other than through the proxy.
- Contacting hosts other than the API and the challenge's websites, or trying to get data out of the sandbox.
- Starting browsers of your own in the sandbox, headless ones included. At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up
  to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start others.
  On your own machine (developing with the scouting logins) your agent starts its own browsers; that is up to you.
- Attacking the platform, the websites, the sandbox or other teams; sharing scored-run data.
## How it is checked
- **Package review before any scored run:** an AI code reviewer, a coding agent that reads your whole package in an
  isolated VM. Outcomes: passed, flagged or rejected (no runs). A flagged package still runs and scores, but its
  result stays off the public leaderboard and the activity feed until an organizer passes it; your team sees it
  marked "flagged: waiting for an organizer". Notes and docs addressed to the reviewer are not evidence of compliance
  and do not count against you on their own. Instructions trying to steer the reviewer's verdict do.
  The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers: your team reads "Flagged by the reviewing agent" or "Rejected by
  the reviewing agent". Someone from Atira looks at flagged packages shortly and unflags a misdetection; if you think
  a reject is one, contact the Atira team.
- **The organizers decide flagged packages, and can look at any submission:** they pass it, add an internal note
  (this changes nothing you or the leaderboard see) or disqualify it. A disqualified submission and its runs read
  "disqualified": it leaves the leaderboard and the final run, its runs still going stop, and your team page shows the
  organizers' reason.
- **Hardcoded values:** the reviewer rejects copied scenario values in code or config, even in defaults or fallbacks.
- **The final run** uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a
  supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software,
  with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently
  across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it. That run weighs most when we pick the
  winners, so build a system that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.
- **The sandbox** reaches only our API and the websites, so every model call passes the proxy and is measured.
  Your team secrets reach only the timed run step and are redacted from its logs.
- **Website logins** exist only for a live run and stop working when it ends.
- **Browsers:** the sandbox stops any browser your agent starts beyond the ones it asked for and notes it in the
  run's logs: `[platform] stopped a browser the agent started`.
- **Everything measured** (tokens, cost, time, the answer) is recorded by the platform, never reported by you.
Breaking these rules gets the submission rejected before it runs, or removed later; repeated or deliberate attempts
get the team disqualified.

A flagged result stays off the public leaderboard until an organizer passes it. **Show flagged** on the leaderboard
lists flagged results, without a rank.

content.text:
**My pick is BMW, with Tacto as a close second. Register on ehl.gg before the challenge-selection deadline at 14:00 CET today, which was about an hour away when I checked.**

I went through the BMW PDF, all of Tacto's arena page and repo (brief, rules, scoring, starter kit), all of Atira's challenge page and fair-play rules, and the EHL finale page. Each track pays €1,500, and the best 2 finalist teams in each track go on to the Grand Final pitch.

## The three challenges

| | **BMW: AI for product decisions** | **Tacto: negotiation arena** | **Atira: win a tender** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What you build** | An app that turns customer feedback, sales and equipment data, and web research into ranked requirements for the next 1, 5 or 7 Series. A product manager reviews, edits, approves or rejects each one. | An AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots for a fictional pump maker. | A browser agent that works through 4 German business sites (tender portal, supplier portal, ERP, webmail) and submits one signed, priced bid. |
| **How it's judged** | A jury. Criteria: decision and scoring logic, human-in-the-loop workflow, traceability, usability, innovation and business impact. | An objective score, total € saved. A Live Final on Sunday at 12:00 runs 5 waves of hidden suppliers, 8 minutes each, with no human in the loop. The top 10 pitch to the jury. | An objective score. Your latest submission runs once on a **private dataset with different websites**. Ranking: eligible first, then quality, then cost × time. |
| **Competition I saw** | Unknown, probably the most popular. | **10 teams** on the practice page | **16 teams** |
| **Model limits** | None | Any LLM you bring, and LLM spend isn't scored | Only through their proxy, and every call adds to your cost |
| **Hard parts** | Nobody wins on a score number, so the demo has to make the jury believe it. I haven't seen the data; BMW hands it out on site. | Reading each supplier from call notes and letters. Hidden cases mix supplier and case types you never practised against. | 29 dense pricing rules down to the cent (currency, metal indices, shared setup pools, bonus bands), plus cookie walls, session timeouts, look-alike e-mails, and different websites in the final. |
| **Starting point** | A two-page brief | A strong Python kit; first agent on the board in 15 minutes | A CLI, a sandbox and scouting logins |

## Why BMW

1. **It fits your track record.** You won Klarblick with an AI app plus a strong demo, and you're a product and UX builder. BMW's criteria (workflow, traceability, usability, business impact) reward exactly that. The other two reward agent-engineering rigour.
2. **Nothing is hidden at the end.** Tacto and Atira both decide the winner with one unseen run you can't watch or fix. A strong 1.5-day agent can still get wrecked by a hidden supplier type or a redesigned website. With BMW, what you demo is what gets judged.
3. **You can scope it.** The brief says outright that you don't need every capability built to the same level. You can go deep on one thing, like an evidence-to-requirement trace view with "evidence vs. assumption" labels and approve/reject controls, and still score well.

**The risk:** BMW is the easiest to start, so it probably draws the most teams, and jury judging is subjective. To stand out, every requirement should be traceable back to a specific feedback quote or data row. Show where sources conflict, and flag uncertainty explicitly. Most teams will build a chat UI over PDFs; don't.

## When to pick Tacto instead

Pick Tacto if your team is mostly backend or agent engineers who enjoy optimisation. With only 10 teams practising, a solid agent nearly guarantees a top-10 pitch slot. The scoring is objective, you get unlimited practice with a full replay after every case, and you can use the best LLM available for free scoring-wise. The brief's own tip is "numbers come from code, the model writes": compute the total cost of every offer in Python, and let the LLM choose the arguments and wording.

## Skip Atira

Skip it unless you have someone strong at browser automation. It needs exact-to-the-cent accuracy across 29 interacting rules, through flaky websites. The final runs on software your agent has never seen, and you're limited to their hosted models with cost × time counted against you. It's the best engineering puzzle of the three and the hardest to win in 30 hours.

Tell me which one you choose and I can start scaffolding right away, for example a Tacto agent from their kit or a BMW app skeleton. I can also put this comparison on a shareable page for your team.

cd "/Users/speak2gokul01/Documents/Intern applications/BMW Hackathon" && python3 - <<'EOF'
import openpyxl, re
from collections import Counter
comp=r'\b(mercedes|benz|audi|tesla|lexus|genesis|porsche|volvo|lucid|cadillac|polestar|byd|nio|vw|volkswagen|hyundai|kia|toyota|range rover|jaguar)\b'
for f in ["F70","G60","G70"]:
    rows=list(openpyxl.load_workbook(f+"_feedback_hackathon.xlsx",read_only=True).worksheets[0].iter_rows(values_only=True))[1:]
    uniq={r[0]:r for r in rows}.values()
    c=Counter(m.lower() for r in uniq for m in re.findall(comp,r[8] or "",re.I))
