input.content:
"""Which part of the car a requirement is about, and which photo shows it.

Each requirement gets: aspect (Cockpit, Interior, Exterior, Driving), part (e.g. "Gear selector"),
photo (web path) and a focal point (x, y in % of the photo) so the web app can crop to that part.
Owner: Arjun. Add rules and focal points as new topics or better photos come in.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

# Photos per vehicle (files live in web/public/cars/<code>/<key>.jpg), with focal points per part.
# Coordinates are percentages of the photo: (x, y).
PHOTOS: dict[str, dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, int]]]] = {
    "F70": {
        "cockpit": {"default": (60, 45), "display": (76, 36), "cluster": (55, 35), "steering": (22, 35), "climate": (75, 55),
                    "console": (62, 84), "gear": (40, 91), "seats": (8, 84)},
        "front": {"default": (45, 55), "grille": (10, 56), "headlight": (37, 53), "mirror": (68, 44), "door": (79, 47), "wheel": (55, 62)},
        "road": {"default": (50, 58), "wheel": (52, 66)},
        "white": {"default": (50, 60), "wheel": (50, 65), "brake": (51, 66), "headlight": (22, 55)},
        "rear": {"default": (55, 55), "boot": (62, 50), "taillight": (68, 52)},
    },
    "G60": {
        "cockpit": {"default": (55, 45), "display": (70, 40), "cluster": (45, 38), "steering": (15, 38), "climate": (60, 52),
                    "console": (50, 85), "gear": (50, 85)},
        "seats": {"default": (55, 55), "seats": (60, 60)},
        "front": {"default": (50, 66), "headlight": (85, 66), "wheel": (65, 72), "mirror": (58, 61), "door": (45, 64)},
        "grille": {"default": (50, 45), "grille": (50, 40)},
        "road": {"default": (50, 50), "wheel": (60, 65)},
    },
    "G70": {
        "cockpit": {"default": (55, 50), "display": (78, 45), "steering": (37, 45), "climate": (70, 30), "console": (55, 85),
                    "gear": (55, 85), "seats": (15, 80), "door": (8, 50)},
        "front": {"default": (51, 55), "grille": (51, 52), "headlight": (35, 49)},
        "detail": {"default": (50, 55), "headlight": (45, 52), "wheel": (95, 60), "grille": (8, 60)},
        "road": {"default": (45, 58), "wheel": (45, 65)},
        "rear": {"default": (50, 58), "boot": (50, 55), "taillight": (35, 52)},
    },
}

# Topic rules, first match wins: (pattern, aspect, part, [(photo, focal key), ...fallbacks]).
RULES: list[tuple[str, str, str, list[tuple[str, str]]]] = [
    (r"touch ?screen|operating concept|control display|idrive", "Cockpit", "Control display", [("cockpit", "display")]),
    (r"instrument cluster|head-up", "Cockpit", "Instrument cluster", [("cockpit", "cluster")]),
    (r"navigation", "Cockpit", "Navigation", [("cockpit", "display")]),
    (r"esim|connected|infotainment|app\b|remote|carplay|android", "Cockpit", "Connectivity", [("cockpit", "display")]),
    (r"assistant|voice", "Cockpit", "Voice assistant", [("cockpit", "display")]),
    (r"audio|sound|radio|speaker", "Cockpit", "Audio", [("cockpit", "display")]),
    (r"climat|air condition|heating|ventilat", "Cockpit", "Climate control", [("cockpit", "climate")]),
    (r"steering wheel|horn", "Cockpit", "Steering wheel", [("cockpit", "steering")]),
    (r"transmission|gear", "Interior", "Gear selector", [("cockpit", "gear")]),
    (r"seat", "Interior", "Seats", [("seats", "seats"), ("cockpit", "seats")]),
    (r"storage|console|usb|wireless charging|mobile device|cup", "Interior", "Centre console", [("cockpit", "console")]),
    (r"ambient|interior design|interior", "Interior", "Interior design", [("cockpit", "default")]),
    (r"space|rear seat|rear entertainment", "Interior", "Cabin space", [("seats", "default"), ("cockpit", "seats")]),
    (r"door|key|access|lock", "Exterior", "Doors and access", [("front", "door"), ("cockpit", "door")]),
    (r"mirror", "Exterior", "Door mirror", [("front", "mirror")]),
    (r"wheel|tyre|tire", "Exterior", "Wheels and tyres", [("white", "wheel"), ("detail", "wheel"), ("front", "wheel"), ("road", "wheel")]),
    (r"brak", "Driving", "Brakes", [("white", "brake"), ("detail", "wheel"), ("road", "wheel")]),
    (r"headlight|light", "Exterior", "Lighting", [("detail", "headlight"), ("front", "headlight")]),
    (r"luggage|trunk|tailgate|boot", "Exterior", "Boot", [("rear", "boot"), ("road", "default")]),
    (r"assistance|highway|parking|camera|sensor|blind spot|collision|lane", "Exterior", "Sensors and assistance",
     [("grille", "grille"), ("front", "grille"), ("detail", "grille")]),
    (r"panorama|roof", "Exterior", "Roof", [("road", "default")]),
    (r"range|charging|electric", "Driving", "Range and charging", [("road", "default")]),
    (r"cushioning|damping|riding|handling|chassis", "Driving", "Ride and handling", [("road", "default")]),
    (r"drivetrain|engine|drive|modes|acceleration", "Driving", "Powertrain", [("road", "default")]),
    (r"acoustic|noise", "Driving", "Quietness", [("road", "default")]),
    (r"exterior|design|paint|body", "Exterior", "Exterior design", [("front", "default"), ("road", "default")]),
]


def for_topic(vehicle: str, topic: str) -> dict:
    photos = PHOTOS.get(vehicle, {})
    t = topic.lower()
    for pattern, aspect, part, options in RULES:
        if re.search(pattern, t):
            for photo, key in options:
                if photo in photos:
                    x, y = photos[photo].get(key, photos[photo]["default"])
                    return {"aspect": aspect, "part": part, "photo": f"/cars/{vehicle}/{photo}.jpg", "focal_x": x, "focal_y": y}
            break
    photo = "front" if "front" in photos else next(iter(photos), None)
    x, y = photos[photo]["default"] if photo else (50, 50)
    return {"aspect": "Vehicle", "part": "Whole vehicle", "photo": f"/cars/{vehicle}/{photo}.jpg" if photo else None,
            "focal_x": x, "focal_y": y}

content.text:
MoSCoW grouping and the photo header (option A) are now in the app. Refresh **http://localhost:3001** to see them. Typecheck and lint pass.

**The list:** requirements are grouped under **Must have** (red), **Should have** (orange), **Could have** (blue) and **Won't have this time** (grey). Each group shows a count and a one-line hint. Each row shows:
- the title and the priority number
- the part of the car it's about, e.g. "Driving · Brakes"
- the Act / Park chip

The quadrant filters on top still work.

**The detail view:** each requirement opens with a photo of its part of the car, cropped to that part. The title sits over it in white with the MoSCoW, quadrant and status chips. Examples:
- Touchscreen → the cockpit display
- Transmission → the gear selector
- Braking → the wheel and red brake caliper (in the screenshot I took)
- Climate control → the 7 Series dashboard

It works for all three cars: each has 5 photos with focal points, 15 in total.

**What else changed:**
- **New pipeline file `aspects.py`**: maps each topic to an aspect, a part, a photo and a focal point. I added it to Arjun's list in TEAM.md.
- **Four new database columns**: aspect, part, photo and focal point. The build now drops and recreates the tables, so after pulling, everyone just runs `uv run pmw build` once.
- **Font loading fix**: Next's built-in font loader crashed after a cache reset, and the same setup left the new colours un-compiled. Albert Sans now loads through a normal stylesheet link, which has no build step to break.

**Known gaps:**
- There's no seat or speaker close-up in the 1 Series price list, so "Durable seats" and "Quieter audio" show the nearest visible part.
- The new files aren't staged yet, so run `git add -A` before your first commit.

# Agent brief: Vishwa (AI lead) · Product Minds on Wheels

You are working on **Product Minds on Wheels (PMW)**, a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge
"AI for Product Decision Making" (EHL Grand Finale 2026). Read this whole brief before changing anything.

## 1. What the product does

PMW helps a BMW product manager decide what the next generation of a vehicle should offer customers.
It turns BMW's customer data into requirements a product manager can defend:

```
Customer voice → Signal → Root cause → Customer need → Requirement → Priority + Confidence → PM decision → Audit trail
```

BMW's judges score: decision and scoring logic, human-in-the-loop workflow, traceability and auditability,
usability and feasibility, innovation and scalability. BMW asked for each requirement to carry: ID,
actionable description, linked findings and sources, priority or score, prioritisation rationale,
evidence level, future-facing assumptions and uncertainties, and decision status.

**Demo vehicle: BMW 7 Series (G70), across all markets.** The 1 Series (F70) and 5 Series (G60) show that
the engine generalises.

## 2. Setup

Repo: https://github.com/Vishwa-Balasubramanian/PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels-

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Vishwa-Balasubramanian/PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels-.git
cd PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels-
brew install poppler            # pdftotext, for the price-list PDFs
cd pipeline && uv sync --extra llm && uv run pmw build      # ~2 seconds, rebuilds db/pmw.sqlite
cd ../web && npm install && npm run dev                     # http://localhost:3000
```

Read `README.md` and `TEAM.md` in the repo first. For LLM calls: `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...`, and the
model comes from `PMW_MODEL` (see `pipeline/.env.example`). Never commit keys or `.env` files. The repo is public.

## 3. How the code is organised

| Path | What | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `data/` | BMW files: 3 feedback xlsx, customer studies, sales, 3 German price-list PDFs | shared, read-only |
| `pipeline/pmw/db.py` | SQLite schema. **The contract with the web app.** | everyone, change together |
| `pipeline/pmw/ingest.py`, `evidence.py`, `scope.py`, `aspects.py` | data, survey cross-checks, scope guard, photos | Arjun |
| `pipeline/pmw/signals.py`, `derive.py`, `score.py` | **signals, requirement drafting, scoring** | **you** |
| `pipeline/pmw/cli.py` | orchestrates the steps (`uv run pmw build`) | shared, keep edits small and additive |
| `pipeline/cache/` | cached LLM outputs, **committed** so teammates without a key get the same drafts | you |
| `web/lib/types.ts` | TypeScript mirror of the schema | everyone, change together |
| `web/lib/gate.ts` | every database read in the web app, filtered by region | shared |
| `web/app/**`, `web/components/**` | UI | Gokul |

Facts about the data you will need:
- Feedback: one row per (comment, label). Stored as `feedback` (one row per comment) + `feedback_labels`.
  F70 2,128 comments, G60 4,000, G70 4,000. Sources: A owner reviews, B dealer notes ("Customer stated…"),
  C quality survey with severity ("I had a serious problem with…"), D open survey answers (always unlabelled).
- **Unlabelled comments** (`feedback.classified = 0`): F70 300, G60 440, G70 440.
- G70 comments: US 3,792, Rest of World 189, Europe 19, **China 0**. The China study gives means only.
- Requirements today: 15 per vehicle, built in **template mode**, so `root_cause` and `customer_need` are NULL
  and titles read like "Easy-to-use personal eSIM". The web app shows "Pending AI analysis" for NULL fields.

## 4. Rules (non-negotiable)

1. **Language from the LLM, numbers from code.** The LLM never writes a score, count or percentage that is
   stored as data. Priority and confidence stay deterministic in `score.py`.
2. **Priority and confidence stay separate.** Quadrants: act / validate / monitor / park.
3. **No invented facts.** Every claim must trace to comment IDs (e.g. `G70-2544`), survey rows or sales rows.
   Prompts must forbid inventing numbers; validate outputs and drop claims that cite unknown IDs.
4. **Scope:** customer-facing product requirements only. Never regulatory, engineering-spec or pricing requirements.
5. **Every AI step writes an audit event** via `db.audit(...)` (`actor_type="ai"`).
6. **Cache every LLM call** in `pipeline/cache/` keyed by inputs, and commit the cache. The build must still
   work with no API key (template or cached output).
7. **Schema changes:** edit `pipeline/pmw/db.py` **and** `web/lib/types.ts` in the same PR, say so in the PR
   title, and tell Gokul and Arjun. Adding columns or JSON fields is fine; never rename or remove.
8. Work on branches `vishwa/<topic>`, small PRs into `main`, pull `main` every two hours.
9. Commit messages: plain and descriptive. No AI tool names, no co-author or attribution lines.
10. Before every PR, both must pass:
    `cd pipeline && uv run pmw build` and `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build`.
11. The web app uses **Next.js 16** with `cacheComponents: false`. If you touch web code, read the relevant
    guide in `web/node_modules/next/dist/docs/` first. Do not put SQL in pages or components; add a function
    to `web/lib/gate.ts`.

## 5. Your tasks, in priority order

### Task 1: AI-written requirements (highest demo value)
File: `pipeline/pmw/derive.py` (the `llm()` function and `PROMPT` exist already).
- Run `uv run pmw build --llm` and iterate on the prompt until, for all 45 requirements:
  `root_cause` and `customer_need` are filled; `title` is at most 9 words, customer-facing, no BMW jargon;
  `requirement` is one or two testable sentences for the successor vehicle; `assumptions` and `uncertainties`
  are concrete; `future_lens` is one of `current_pain | emerging | future_must_have`.
- Root causes should cite comment IDs from the quotes you passed in. Reject outputs citing IDs not in the input.
- Validate the JSON keys, retry once on bad JSON, fall back to the template on failure (and log it).
- Commit `pipeline/cache/derive_*.json`.
- **Done when:** the 7 Series cards in the app read like a BMW product manager wrote them, and a teammate
  without an API key gets the same text after `uv run pmw build --llm`.

### Task 2: Label the unlabelled comments
File: `pipeline/pmw/signals.py`, function `classify_unlabelled(con, vehicle)` (stub returns 0).
- Send comments with `classified = 0` in batches (~40) with the list of topics already used for that vehicle
  (`SELECT DISTINCT topic FROM feedback_labels ...`) and the four feedback types.
- Insert into `feedback_labels` with `label_source = 'ai'`. Allow "none" when nothing fits; do not force a label.
- Use a cheaper/faster model for this bulk step if available (e.g. a `PMW_MODEL_FAST` env var).
- One audit event per batch. Cache per batch. Update the data-issue text so it reports how many were labelled.
- Check: `signals.build` already joins all labels, so AI labels flow into the counts automatically.
- **Done when:** unlabelled counts drop substantially and Data health shows how many comments the AI labelled.

### Task 3: Calibrate scoring for a convincing demo
File: `pipeline/pmw/score.py` (`DEFAULT_WEIGHTS`, thresholds, factor formulas).
- Today the G70 split is act 9, validate 0, monitor 2, park 4. Aim for **at least two requirements in every
  quadrant for the 7 Series** after Tasks 1 and 2, without making the formulas arbitrary.
- Write the reasoning for every weight and threshold as a comment next to it. Judges will ask.
- The MoSCoW groups in the UI use priority cut-offs 65 / 55 / 45 (`MOSCOW` in `web/components/ui.tsx`).
  If you move the priority threshold, tell Gokul so the two stay consistent.

### Task 4: Challenge narrative
Files: `pipeline/pmw/score.py` (`challenge_issues`), `pipeline/pmw/cli.py`.
- Keep the deterministic issues and penalties. Add an LLM paragraph "What could make this wrong" to the
  challenge JSON as a new optional field `narrative` (cached, built at pipeline time, no runtime LLM call).
- Add `narrative?: string` to the `Challenge` type in `web/lib/types.ts`. Gokul renders it; if you add the
  render yourself, keep it to a few lines in the "Challenge result" section of `web/components/DecisionCard.tsx`
  and say so in the PR.

### Task 5: Merge narrow topics into real themes
File: `pipeline/pmw/signals.py`.
- BMW's labels are narrow: climate is spread over "Vehicle, climatization", "Air conditioning, setting" and
  "Air conditioning control panel"; connectivity over "Personal eSIM", "My BMW App / MINI App",
  "ConnectedDrive and Infotainment, overall technology", "Apple CarPlay".
- Propose a theme map with the LLM, review it yourself, and commit it as a **static** dict (so builds are
  deterministic). Build one signal per theme. Keep `evidence.TOPIC_TO_SURVEY` working for every member topic
  (coordinate with Arjun, who owns that map).
- Check that `aspects.for_topic` still finds the right photo for a theme (Arjun owns `aspects.py`).

## 6. How to check your work in the app

- `http://localhost:3000/vehicles/G70`: the requirement list (MoSCoW groups) and the Decision Card.
- Use **Challenge** on a requirement: confidence must drop and the audit trail must show each step.
- `?view=data` (Data health) for data issues; `/audit` for the full log.
- Region picker (top right): switching to China must hide US comments and log the access.

## 7. When you are done with a task

Open a PR with: what changed, before/after for two G70 requirements (title, root cause, requirement),
the new quadrant split, and any schema change called out in the title.

  `already_exists TEXT` (JSON) to `requirements`. Matches that are not one of the top-15 signals become their own

  - G60: wireless charging pad is **standard** yet ~11 owners report it defective → `standard_but_failing`.
  - F70: comfort access exists but only inside optional packages.

### Task 2: Equipment parser good enough for Task 1
File: `pipeline/pmw/ingest.py` (`ingest_equipment`).

- Write a small check that asserts the verified facts above (7VB €2,750 contains Aktive Sitzbelüftung vorn;

### Task 3: Market conflict cards
File: `pipeline/pmw/evidence.py` (`build_conflicts` exists).
- In-scope China vs Europe gaps for the 7 Series (CN vs EU means): front interior roominess 7.69 vs 9.69,

File: `pipeline/pmw/aspects.py` (photos live in `web/public/cars/<vehicle>/<key>.jpg`, focal points in `PHOTOS`).

Yes, as long as their agent can run commands on their machine. I checked the repo:

- **Arjun** (`arjunselvakumar93`) already has write access, so his agent can push branches and open PRs.
- **Vishwa** owns the repo.
- There's also a fourth collaborator with write access, `gi60wedo`. Make sure you know who that is.

**What each of them needs:**
1. **A coding agent with terminal access**, e.g. Claude Code, Cursor or Codex. A plain chat window can't run git or the app.
2. **On their machine:** git, Node 20+, uv and poppler. The setup commands are in the brief.
3. **GitHub login:** `gh auth login` once, so the agent can run `gh pr create`. Without it, the agent pushes the branch and they open the PR on github.com.
4. **Vishwa only:** an LLM API key for his tasks. Arjun's tasks mostly don't need one.

**What to type into the agent:**
> Read `VISHWA_AGENT_BRIEF.md`, then do **Task 1 only**. Work on a new branch, run both checks from the rules, push, open a PR, then stop and report.

One task per run works better than "do everything": smaller PRs, easier review, fewer conflicts.

**One safety gap, partly fixed:** `main` has no branch protection right now, so any agent with write access *could* push straight to it. I added two rules to both briefs: **never push to `main` directly and never merge your own PR**, and **work on one task at a time, then stop and report**. Agents usually follow that. To make it impossible rather than just discouraged, Vishwa can turn on protection in Settings → Branches → add a rule for `main` → "Require a pull request before merging".

**Review before merging.** PRs that change `db.py` or `types.ts` affect all three of you; the briefs tell the agents to flag those in the PR title. After merging one of those, everyone pulls and runs `uv run pmw build` once.

Each option accepts an object whose keys are **route globs** (matched with [picomatch](https://www.npmjs.com/package/picomatch#basic-globbing) against the route path, e.g. `/api/hello`) and whose values are **glob patterns resolved from the project root** that specify files to include or exclude in the trace.

questions.question: How should the hosted demo store PM decisions (approve, edit, challenge, audit trail)?

options.label: Turso, hosted SQLite (Recommended)
options.description: Free tier, added through the Vercel Marketplace with your Vercel login. Same SQL as now, one code path locally and online. I'd refactor the data layer (~1–2 h) and add a command that uploads the pipeline's database. Decisions persist and are shared by everyone using the link.

options.label: Read-only hosted demo
options.description: No new services. The hosted site shows everything but disables the decision buttons with a note; decisions only work when run locally (e.g. for the live demo from your laptop). About 15 minutes.

options.label: Vercel Blob overlay
options.description: Stays inside your Vercel account (no new provider). Base data stays in the bundled SQLite; decisions and audit events go to a JSON log in Blob storage. Works, but it's a custom layer the team must maintain, and it's weaker under simultaneous edits.

The app is live at **https://product-minds-on-wheels.vercel.app**

**No indexing:**
- every page has `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`
- `robots.txt` blocks all crawlers
- every response carries the `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nosnippet, noimageindex` header

I checked all three on the live site.

**No trackers:**
- no Vercel Analytics, no Speed Insights, no third-party scripts
- the font is now hosted with the app, so visitors' browsers make **zero** requests to Google or anyone else; I checked the live HTML
- I also removed the `X-Powered-By` header

**What I had to change:**
- **The database moved to Turso,** a hosted SQLite on the free Starter plan ($0), added through your Vercel account in the US-East region, next to the app. The first deploy showed that Vercel runs each page and the decision API as separate servers, so decisions saved in one were invisible to the others. Now Approve / Edit / Challenge persist and appear in the audit trail for everyone using the link; I tested this on the live site.
- **Same code locally and online:** on your laptop the app still reads the local `db/pmw.sqlite`. Vercel uses Turso.
- **`npm run db:push`** uploads the pipeline's database to the live site in about 20 seconds. I used it to reset the live demo to a clean state after testing. **It overwrites any decisions made online.**
- **The live site doesn't auto-deploy from GitHub.** Pushes won't break it; to update, run `vercel deploy --prod` from `web/`.

**Things to know:**
- **Anyone with the link can open it,** including the BMW data, same as the public GitHub repo. It just won't show up in search engines. If you want a password, Vercel can add one (on paid plans), or I can add a simple shared access code to the app.
- **The first visit after idle takes ~4 seconds,** while Vercel wakes up. Open the link once before the live demo.
- **These changes are local only, not on GitHub yet.** The data layer (`web/lib/gate.ts`) is now async, so Vishwa's and Arjun's agents should start from this version or their code will conflict. Should I commit and push it now?
Also add our latest plan.md to github

# Plan · Product Minds on Wheels (PMW)

Latest team plan for the BMW track at the EHL Grand Finale 2026. Updated 10 October 2026, evening.
Setup and code layout: [README.md](README.md). Who owns what: [TEAM.md](TEAM.md). Agent briefs: [docs/agent-briefs/](docs/agent-briefs/).

## 1. The challenge in one line

Help a BMW product manager decide what the next generation of a car must offer customers, prove why, and
record every decision. BMW judges: decision and scoring logic, workflow and human decision-making, traceability
and auditability, usability and feasibility, innovation and business impact. Deliverables: pitch deck,
GitHub repository, live demo.

## 2. What we are building

A web app where AI turns BMW's customer data into a ranked list of requirements for the next generation, shows
the evidence behind each one, and leaves every decision to the product manager.

```
Customer voice → Signal → Root cause → Customer need → Requirement → Priority + Confidence → PM decision → Audit trail
```

## 3. Decisions made

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Name | **Product Minds on Wheels (PMW)** |
| Demo vehicle | **BMW 7 Series (G70), across all markets.** 1 Series and 5 Series show the engine generalises. |
| App type | Custom web app (Next.js) with a Python pipeline inside. Not Streamlit. |
| Look and feel | bmw.de: photography first, light body type, uppercase headlines, square buttons, one blue. Real car photos from the BMW price lists. |
| Home screen | Three cars side by side as lanes (1, 5, 7 Series), real photos, a 1-second entrance, no long animation. |
| Login | **None.** An Amazon-style region picker (United States, Europe, China, Rest of World, All markets). SSO is explained in the pitch. |
| Access | A market PM sees raw customer comments from their own market only; summary scores stay visible; access is logged. |
| Scoring | **Priority and confidence are separate**, both computed by code. Decision quadrants: Act, Validate first, Monitor, Park. |
| Priority display | **MoSCoW groups**: Must have 65+, Should have 55+, Could have 45+, Won't have this time below 45. |
| Requirement view | **Photo header**: each requirement opens on a photo of the part of the car it is about, cropped to that part. |
| Data store | SQLite locally; Turso (hosted SQLite) for the live demo. |
| Hosting | Vercel, **not indexed by search engines, no trackers, no third-party requests**. |

## 4. Signature features (the "wow")

1. **You already sell this.** Customers ask for features BMW already offers as an option, inside a package, or as
   standard on another BMW (Trickle-Down). Verified examples: ventilated seats only inside the 5 Series Comfort
   Package 7VB (€2,750); 7 Series has multifunction seats and comfort access as standard.
2. **Challenge.** The PM asks "what could make this wrong?", the red-team check lists the issues and confidence
   drops live (for example 73 → 53 when 97% of the evidence comes from one market).
3. **One click from requirement to customer.** Real quotes with comment IDs, source and severity.
4. **Evidence versus assumption.** Every requirement separates today's data from assumptions about 2030.
5. **Conflict alerts and missing voices.** For the 7 Series, 95% of comments come from the US, which buys 29%
   of the cars, and China has none. China and Europe disagree on rear roominess (7.52 vs 9.41), front roominess
   (7.69 vs 9.69) and braking (7.82 vs 9.60).
6. **Scope guard.** Pricing, regulatory and engineering topics are filtered out with a stated reason
   (for example permanent start-stop switch-off touches emissions regulation).
7. **Happiness Meter** (stretch). Share of customer pain addressed per market as the PM approves, weighted by sales.

## 5. Status

**Done**
- Pipeline: ingest with recorded data issues, signals, scope guard, survey cross-checks, missing voices, market
  conflicts, template requirements, deterministic priority and confidence, challenge issues, photo per requirement.
- Web app: home, region picker, MoSCoW requirement list, Decision Card with photo header and the 5-step ladder,
  approve / validate first / edit / reject / challenge, decision matrix, signals, data health, audit trail.
- Hosted at https://product-minds-on-wheels.vercel.app with a shared database, so decisions persist.
- Agent briefs for Vishwa and Arjun in the repo.

**In progress**
- Arjun: "You already sell this" finder (pull request #1 open).
- Vishwa: AI-written root cause, customer need and requirement text (templates show "Pending AI analysis" today).

**Open**
- Gokul: priority weight sliders and strategy presets, requirement export in BMW's format, workflow page,
  "You already sell this" banner, challenge narrative display, Happiness Meter UI, pitch deck.
- Arjun: equipment parser, market conflict cards, Happiness Meter data, survey coverage, photos, web sources.
- Vishwa: label the ~1,180 unlabelled comments, scoring calibration, challenge narrative, theme merging.

## 6. Demo story (5 minutes, 7 Series)

1. Home: three cars, region United States. The 1 Series is greyed out: not sold in the US.
2. Open the 7 Series: the missing-voices warning.
3. A requirement: photo of the part, customer voice, signal, root cause, need, requirement, real quotes with IDs.
4. Priority and confidence side by side, every factor explained, its place in the decision matrix.
5. **Challenge**: confidence drops and the requirement moves from Act to Validate first.
6. Edit, then approve with a reason. Show the audit trail.
7. **You already sell this** on a quick-win requirement.
8. Switch region to China: thin evidence, US comments restricted, the access is logged.
9. Data health: the traps in BMW's data and how we handled them.

Pitch lines: "Language reasoning comes from AI. Decision metrics come from deterministic computation."
"PMW helps BMW make product decisions they can defend, not just AI suggestions they have to trust."

## 7. Rules for everyone

- Numbers from code, words from the LLM. No invented facts; every claim traces to a comment ID or data row.
- Customer-facing requirements only: no regulatory, engineering-spec or pricing requirements.
- Schema changes (`pipeline/pmw/db.py` + `web/lib/types.ts`) are agreed by all three.
- All web data access goes through `web/lib/gate.ts` (async since the move to Turso).
- Branches per person, pull requests into `main`, nobody merges their own pull request.
- Feature freeze two hours before the deadline, then rehearse the demo at least five times.

## 8. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Many teams build a chatbot over PDFs | Lead with Challenge, "You already sell this" and the audit trail |
| AI text sounds generic or invents facts | Prompts cite comment IDs; outputs referencing unknown IDs are dropped |
| Thin data for China, Germany-only price lists | Shown openly as assumptions and lower confidence |
| Live demo network or cold start | Open the hosted link once beforehand; keep the local version ready as backup |
| Repo and site are public with BMW data | Not indexed; check the hackathon terms on sharing |

content.text:
PLAN.md is on GitHub, together with the hosting changes, and the live site is up to date.

**About PLAN.md:** I couldn't find an existing plan.md for the hackathon. The only ones on your machine are from May to September and unrelated. So I wrote **PLAN.md** from everything we've agreed: the challenge, the decisions table, the signature features, current status, the demo story, rules and risks. TEAM.md links to it. Tell me if you meant a different file and I'll swap it in.

**What I pushed:**
- `8536780`: Vercel hosting, the shared database, no indexing, the self-hosted font.
- `17f2266`: PLAN.md.

Both are authored as Gokul Rajan with no AI mentions. Someone had pushed in the meantime, so I put our commits on top of theirs and resolved one overlapping line.

**Arjun merged his own PR** ("You already sell this", #1) while I was working. It works with our changes: I rebuilt everything, and the build, typecheck and live site all pass. The live site now includes his 221 equipment matches. Two things to raise with the team:

1. **The briefs say nobody merges their own PR.** Turning on branch protection for `main` (Vishwa: Settings → Branches) makes that a rule rather than a request.
2. **His change grew the requirement lists a lot:** 7 Series 15 → 39, 5 Series 15 → 60, 1 Series 15 → 38. Most of the new ones are "quick wins" landing in Park, which buries the strong items in the demo. I'd suggest a separate "Quick wins" filter or a cap. That's a team decision.

**What's still open on your side:** the "You already sell this" data is now in the database, but the Decision Card doesn't show it yet. That banner is your UI task.

**Tell Vishwa and Arjun to `git pull` now.** The data layer is async, so new data functions in `web/lib/gate.ts` must use `await`; the brief and PLAN.md both say so.
Review Arjun's PR and if everything checks out, merge it with our main branch

 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from .config import MARKETS
+from . import db
+
+# English customer language to German option-list wording. Terms are intentionally
+# narrow: a match is emitted only when the same phrase is present in a comment
+# and an equipment row, so a topic-level similarity never becomes a claimed fact.
+EQUIPMENT_GLOSSARY = {
+    "ventilated seats": ("ventilat", "sitzbelüftung", "sitzbelueftung"),
+    "comfort access": ("comfort access", "keyless", "komfortzugang"),
+    "multi-contour seats": ("multi-contour", "multi contour", "multicontour", "multifunktionssitze"),
+    "surround view": ("surround view", "surround view system", "surround-view"),
+    "wireless charging": ("wireless charging", "wireless charger", "wireless charging ablage", "induktive lade"),
+    "massage seats": ("massage",),
+    "heated steering wheel": ("heated steering wheel", "lenkradheizung"),
+    "head-up display": ("head-up display", "head up display"),
+    "sun blinds": ("sun blind", "sonnenschutzrollo"),
+    "ambient lighting": ("ambient light", "ambientes licht"),
+}
+
+
+def build_equipment_matches(con, vehicle: str) -> None:
+    """Link only literal bilingual comment/equipment matches, retaining IDs and source rows."""
+    con.execute("DELETE FROM equipment_matches WHERE vehicle = ?", (vehicle,))
+    sigs = con.execute("SELECT id, topic FROM signals WHERE vehicle = ? AND in_scope = 1", (vehicle,)).fetchall()
+    for sig in sigs:
+        feedback = con.execute(
+            "SELECT DISTINCT f.id, f.text FROM feedback f JOIN feedback_labels l ON l.feedback_id=f.id "
+            "WHERE f.vehicle=? AND l.topic=? AND l.feedback_type IN ('Wants','Difficult to Use','Defect')",
+            (vehicle, sig["topic"])).fetchall()
+        if not feedback:
+            continue
+        for english, terms in EQUIPMENT_GLOSSARY.items():
+            hits = [f for f in feedback if any(t in f["text"].casefold() for t in terms if " " in t or len(t) > 6)]
+            if not hits:
+                continue
+            pending = {}
+            rows = con.execute("SELECT * FROM equipment WHERE vehicle=?", (vehicle,)).fetchall()
+            for row in rows:
+                name = (row["name"] or "").casefold()
+                if not any(t in name for t in terms):
+                    continue
+                failing_words = ("broken", "defective", "does not work", "not working", "malfunction",
+                                 "doesn't work", "stopped working", "not charging", "won't charge", "faulty")
+                failing_hits = [f for f in hits if any(w in f["text"].casefold() for w in failing_words)]
+                failing = english == "wireless charging" and row["availability"] == "standard" and bool(failing_hits)
+                match_type = ("standard_but_failing" if failing else
+                              "package_same_vehicle" if row["availability"] == "package_item" else
+                              "option_same_vehicle" if row["availability"] == "optional" else None)
+                if match_type is None:
+                    continue
+                matched_hits = failing_hits if failing else hits
+                ids = sorted({f["id"] for f in matched_hits})
+                name_clean = row["name"].lstrip("–- ").strip()
+                item_code, item_price = row["code"], row["price_eur"]
+                package_note = ""
+                if row["availability"] == "package_item" and row["package"]:
+                    parent = con.execute("SELECT name,code,price_eur FROM equipment WHERE vehicle=? AND lower(name)=lower(?) "
+                                         "AND code IS NOT NULL ORDER BY price_eur DESC LIMIT 1", (vehicle, row["package"])).fetchone()
+                    if parent:
+                        item_code, item_price = parent["code"], parent["price_eur"]
+                        package_note = f" Package: {parent['name']} ({parent['code']}, €{parent['price_eur']:,.0f})."
+                note = f"Customer wording '{english}' matches the German equipment row '{name_clean}'.{package_note} Price list: Germany, July 2026."
+                key = (match_type, name_clean, item_code, item_price, vehicle)
+                pending.setdefault(key, {"ids": set(), "note": note})["ids"].update(ids)
+            # A standard feature on another BMW is a trickle-down candidate.
+            for other in con.execute("SELECT * FROM equipment WHERE vehicle<>? AND availability='standard'", (vehicle,)).fetchall():
+                name = (other["name"] or "").casefold()
+                if any(t in name for t in terms):
+                    ids = sorted({f["id"] for f in hits})
+                    name_clean = other["name"].lstrip("–- ").strip()
+                    key = ("standard_other_vehicle", name_clean, other["code"], other["price_eur"], other["vehicle"])
+                    pending.setdefault(key, {"ids": set(), "note":
+                        f"{name_clean} is marked standard on {other['vehicle']} in its German price list."})["ids"].update(ids)
+            for (match_type, name, option_code, price, source_vehicle), values in pending.items():
+                ids = sorted(values["ids"])
+                con.execute("INSERT INTO equipment_matches VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
+                            (vehicle, sig["id"], match_type, name, option_code, price, source_vehicle,
+                             db.dumps(ids), values["note"]))
+                db.audit(con, actor_type="system", actor="Pipeline", entity_type="signal", entity_id=sig["id"],
+                         action="matched customer evidence to equipment", after=f"{match_type}: {name}",
+                         rationale=f"Comment IDs: {', '.join(ids)}; source equipment row retained in equipment.raw")
 
 # BMW topic (taxonomy level 2) -> survey attributes. Prefix match, case-insensitive.
 # "us" = US_2025 questions, "cneu" = CN_EU_2025 attributes.

content.text:
I've finished the review. **The PR was already merged by Arjun himself**, 87 seconds after he opened it, with no description and no review, so there's nothing left to merge. Here's what's in `main` because of it.

## What's good
- **The new PDF parser works:** it reads option codes, prices and package contents from the price-list layout. It also no longer needs poppler installed.
- **It checks itself:** the build fails loudly if the six hand-verified facts stop parsing, e.g. Comfort Package 7VB at €2,750 containing ventilated seats, or the 7 Series multifunction seats being standard. All six pass.
- **The clear cases are right:** the 5 Series "Seating, ventilate / heat" signal matches the Comfort Package from 4 real comments, and "Surround View" matches the Innovation Package 7EW (€2,400).
- **Matching is literal, with an audit trail:** a match needs the same phrase in a comment and in a price-list row, comment IDs are kept, and every match is logged.
- **The web change is one line** and works with the new database layer.

## Problems (the first three would show up in the demo)

1. **Matches leak onto unrelated topics.** A long review that mentions ventilated seats is labelled with many topics, and the match attaches to every one of them. So "You already sell this: ventilated seats, Comfort Package" appears on **Drivetrain, Glove box, Run-flat tyres, Apple CarPlay, Rear view camera** and more. One comment (G60-2467) feeds 9 different topics. On the 7 Series, the **massage seats** package shows up under **Electric Range** and **Touch screen**.

2. **The "quick wins" aren't really quick wins.** Every topic with any match becomes its own generic requirement, e.g. "Easy-to-use climate control panel", while the photo header and text say nothing about the existing option. That's **92 extra requirements** (5 Series: 45, 1 Series: 23, 7 Series: 24), and **81 of them land in Park**, burying the real list. A real quick win should read "Offer ventilated front seats without the €2,750 Comfort Package": one per feature, not one per topic.

3. **Complaints are treated as wishes.** Of the comments behind the option and package matches, only **40 are "Wants"**; **81 are complaints** (64 "hard to use", 17 defects). Someone complaining that their keyless entry is fiddly already has it, so "you already sell this" is the wrong message. Complaints about existing features should become "standard but failing", which right now only works for wireless charging (it's hard-coded).

4. **Smaller issues:**
   - the old parser is left behind as unused code
   - the new "trim" column stores page positions (`col_412`), not trim names
   - the README still says poppler is required

5. **Process:**
   - the PR was self-merged against the brief
   - it changed the shared schema without flagging it in the title

## My recommendation
**Fix forward rather than revert.** The parser and the verified facts are worth keeping. The fixes for 1–3 are contained to the matching step:
- attach a match only to the topic the feature belongs to
- only "Wants" create option, package or other-BMW matches; complaints about standard features become "standard but failing"
- build one quick-win requirement per feature, with its own title, capped at the top ~5 per car

How do you want to handle it?
- **A:** I make these fixes now on a branch, open a PR, and you merge it.
- **B:** I post this review as a comment on Arjun's PR (from your GitHub account), and his agent fixes it.
B

## Review of #1 (post-merge)

Thanks Arjun, the parser and the finder are a strong base. This was merged before review, so here are the findings as follow-ups. Please fix them in a new PR (branch `arjun/fix-equipment-matches`) and let someone else merge it.

### Keep
- Positioned PDF parser (codes, prices, package contents), no Poppler needed.
- `validate_equipment_facts`: all six hand-verified checks pass. Great guard.
- Clear cases are right: G60 "Seating, ventilate / heat" → Comfort Paket 7VB (€2,750, 4 comments) and G60 "Surround View" → 7EW (€2,400, `G60-0513`).
- Literal bilingual matching, comment IDs kept, audit event per match. Web change is compatible with the async `gate.ts` on main.

### Must fix (these show up in the demo)

**1. Matches leak onto unrelated topics.**
A long multi-topic comment that mentions a feature attaches the match to every topic that comment is labelled with. Examples on main:
- G60 "ventilated seats → 7VB" is attached to Drivetrain, Glove box, RSC tire, Apple CarPlay, Rear view camera, Exterior, Driver profile (via `G60-3993`, `G60-3621`, `G60-1946`).
- G70 massage seats (9DA / 9DC) are attached to Electric Range and Touch screen, operation.
- `G60-2467` feeds 9 different topics.

Fix: attach a match only to the topic the feature belongs to. For example, give each glossary entry the topics it may attach to (ventilated seats → seat / climate topics, surround view → camera / parking topics), and otherwise skip it.
Check: `SELECT j.value, COUNT(DISTINCT m.signal_or_requirement_id) FROM equipment_matches m, json_each(m.feedback_ids) j GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5;` should show at most 1 to 2 topics per comment.

**2. Quick-win requirements are generic topic requirements.**
Every signal with any match becomes a requirement such as "Easy-to-use climate control panel", whose title and text say nothing about the existing equipment. That adds 92 requirements (G60 45, F70 23, G70 24), and 81 of them land in Park, which buries the real list.

Fix: build **one quick-win requirement per feature**, not per topic, with its own title and text, e.g. "Offer ventilated front seats without the €2,750 Comfort Package" or "Bring standard comfort access from the 7 Series to the 5 Series". Keep the top ~5 per vehicle (by number of distinct wishing customers). Leave the 15 signal requirements unchanged.

**3. Complaints are treated as wishes.**
Behind the option and package matches there are 40 "Wants" but 64 "Difficult to Use" and 17 "Defect" comments. A customer complaining that keyless entry is fiddly already has it, so "you already sell this" is wrong.

Fix: only `Wants` create `option_same_vehicle`, `package_same_vehicle` and `standard_other_vehicle` matches. `Difficult to Use` / `Defect` on equipment that is standard on that vehicle become `standard_but_failing`, for every glossary entry (today it is hard-coded to wireless charging).

### Smaller
- Remove `_ingest_equipment_legacy` (unused) and the imports only it needs.
- `equipment.trim` stores x positions (`col_412`). Map them to trim names from the column header, or drop the column for now.
- README still says Poppler is required. Update the setup line.
- Next time: flag schema changes (`db.py` / `types.ts`) in the PR title and add a description.

### Done when
- `cd pipeline && uv run pmw build` passes, including `validate_equipment_facts`.
- Requirement counts are back near 15 + up to 5 quick wins per vehicle.
- Every quick win names the feature and its option code or source vehicle, and links its comment IDs.
- `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` passes.

# Agent brief: Gokul (product, frontend and demo lead) · Product Minds on Wheels

You are working on **Product Minds on Wheels (PMW)**, a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge
"AI for Product Decision Making" (EHL Grand Finale 2026). Read this whole brief, `PLAN.md`, `README.md` and
`TEAM.md` before changing anything.

## 1. What the product does

PMW helps a BMW product manager decide what the next generation of a vehicle should offer customers.
It turns BMW's customer data into requirements a product manager can defend:

```
Customer voice → Signal → Root cause → Customer need → Requirement → Priority + Confidence → PM decision → Audit trail
```

BMW's judges score: decision and scoring logic, human-in-the-loop workflow, traceability and auditability,
usability and feasibility, innovation and scalability. Submission: **pitch deck, GitHub repository, live demo.**
BMW's four deliverables: a working prototype; a structured requirement list (ID, description, findings and
sources, priority or score, prioritisation rationale, evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, decision
status); an end-to-end workflow showing what the AI does alone and where human review is mandatory; an audit trail.

**Demo vehicle: BMW 7 Series (G70), across all markets.**

## 2. Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Vishwa-Balasubramanian/PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels-.git
cd PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels-
cd pipeline && uv sync && uv run pmw build      # rebuilds db/pmw.sqlite (~5 s)
cd ../web && npm install && npm run dev         # http://localhost:3000
```

Live demo: https://product-minds-on-wheels.vercel.app (Vercel project `product-minds-on-wheels`, team
`gokul-rajan-s-projects`, **not** connected to GitHub).
- Deploy code: `cd web && vercel deploy --prod`
- Update hosted data: `cd web && vercel env pull .env.local && npm run db:push` (replaces all hosted data,
  including decisions made online)

## 3. How the web app is built (you own `web/app/**` and `web/components/**`)

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `web/app/page.tsx` | Home: three cars as photo panels, live stats per region |
| `web/app/vehicles/[code]/page.tsx` | Vehicle page with tabs: Requirements (MoSCoW list + Decision Card), Decision matrix, Signals, Data health |
| `web/app/audit/page.tsx` | Full audit trail with filters |
| `web/app/api/requirements/[id]/route.ts` | POST approve / reject / validate / edit / challenge / reopen |
| `web/app/api/region/route.ts` | Region picker cookie (stands in for single sign-on) |
| `web/components/DecisionCard.tsx` | The core screen: photo header, ladder, priority, confidence, evidence, survey, assumptions, audit |
| `web/components/DecisionActions.tsx` | Decision buttons and forms (client component) |
| `web/components/ui.tsx` | `MOSCOW` groups (65 / 55 / 45), badges, `FactorBars`, `Matrix`, `AuditTimeline`, `Section` |
| `web/components/Header.tsx`, `RegionPicker.tsx` | Header and Amazon-style region picker |
| `web/lib/gate.ts` | **Every database read**, filtered by the viewer's region. Shared with Vishwa and Arjun. |
| `web/lib/actions.ts` | Every PM decision, written atomically with its audit events (`writeBatch`) |
| `web/lib/db.ts` | libSQL client: local SQLite file in development, hosted Turso on Vercel. Helpers `all`, `one`, `writeBatch` |
| `web/lib/types.ts` | Mirror of the schema in `pipeline/pmw/db.py` |
| `web/app/globals.css` | Design tokens (Tailwind v4 `@theme`) and utilities (`btn-primary`, `btn-outline`, `headline`, `eyebrow`, `container-x`) |

Design language: bmw.de. Photography first, light 300-weight body, uppercase bold headlines, square buttons,
one blue (`--color-blue`). Requirement list = MoSCoW groups. Decision Card = photo header cropped to the part.

## 4. Rules (non-negotiable)

1. **No SQL in pages or components.** Add an `async` function to `web/lib/gate.ts`. Every read respects the
   viewer's region (see `listRequirements`, `getRequirement`). Writes go through `web/lib/actions.ts` and always
   include an audit event in the same `writeBatch`.
2. **Numbers from code, words from the LLM.** Priority and confidence stay separate and deterministic.
3. **Next.js 16** with `cacheComponents: false`; pages use `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`. Read the
   relevant guide in `web/node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using an API you have not used in this version.
   Use the generated `PageProps<...>` / `RouteContext<...>` helpers; `params` and `searchParams` are promises.
4. **Do not use `next/font/google`.** It broke under Turbopack. The font is self-hosted in `public/fonts`.
5. **Keep the site private from search engines and trackers:** no analytics, no third-party scripts, fonts or
   images; keep `robots` metadata, `app/robots.ts` and the `X-Robots-Tag` header.
6. **Schema changes** (`pipeline/pmw/db.py` + `web/lib/types.ts`) are agreed by all three and flagged in the PR title.
7. Work on branches `gokul/<topic>`, small PRs into `main`. Commit messages plain, no AI tool names, no co-author lines.
8. Before every PR and every deploy: `cd pipeline && uv run pmw build` and
   `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint app components lib && npm run build` all pass.

## 5. Your tasks, in priority order

### Task 1: Requirement export (BMW deliverable 2)
- Route handler `GET /api/export?vehicle=G70&format=csv|json`, plus an **Export** button on the vehicle page.
- One row per requirement visible in the viewer's region, with BMW's fields:
  `id`, `title`, `description` (requirement text), `customer_need`, `root_cause`, `findings_and_sources`
  (signal text, top comment IDs from `signal_evidence`, survey rows), `priority`, `moscow`, `priority_rationale`
  (each factor's value, weight and note), `confidence`, `evidence_level` (quadrant + confidence factors),
  `assumptions`, `uncertainties`, `contradictions`, `decision_status`, `last_decision` (actor, time, reason from
  the audit trail), `markets`.
- Restricted markets: export summary fields only, never raw comment text the viewer may not see.
- Log an audit event `exported requirement list` (actor, region, vehicle, format).
- **Done when:** the CSV opens cleanly in Excel and every BMW field is present for all 7 Series requirements.

### Task 2: Workflow page (BMW deliverable 3)
- New page `/workflow`, linked from the header.
- The pipeline as a sequence: Ingest → Signals → Cross-check → Scope guard → Draft requirement → Score →
  **PM decision** → Audit. For each step: what happens, who does it (AI / code / **human, mandatory**), the
  file that does it, and live counts from the database (e.g. 4,000 comments → 549 signals → 15 requirements →
  N decided).
- Make the mandatory human gates visually unmistakable: deciding, challenging, market conflicts, low-confidence items.
- **Done when:** a judge understands in 20 seconds where the AI stops and the product manager decides.

### Task 3: Priority weight sliders and strategy presets
- On the vehicle page: sliders for the five priority factors (`impact`, `frequency`, `market`, `competitive`,
  `future`; labels in the `factor_labels` setting) and presets: Customer first, Premium experience, Quick wins,
  China focus, Europe focus.
- Each requirement stores its factor values in `priority_factors` (`value` 0..1, `weight`, `note`).
  Recompute priority as `round(100 * Σ weight × value / Σ weight)` in a new `web/lib/score.ts`, re-group the
  MoSCoW list and recompute quadrants with the thresholds from `getWeights()`.
- Persist the active weights (e.g. `settings` key `weights_active`) through a new action in `actions.ts`, with an
  audit event (`entity_type = 'weights'`, before/after, reason). Show "Ranking changed by … at …" above the list.
- **Done when:** moving a slider re-ranks the 7 Series live, the change appears in `/audit`, and a reload keeps it.

### Task 4: "You already sell this" banner (after Arjun's fix to PR #1 lands)
- Data: `requirement.kind` (`signal | quick_win | market_conflict`) and `requirement.already_exists`
  (`EquipmentMatch[]`: `match_type`, `equipment_name`, `code`, `price_eur`, `source_vehicle`, `feedback_ids`, `note`).
- Banner on the Decision Card under the photo header, wording per `match_type`:
  option on this car · inside a package (name, code, price) · standard on another BMW · standard but failing.
  Link the comment IDs. A "Quick wins" chip in the list for `kind = 'quick_win'`.
- Wait for Arjun's fix before demoing: today some matches sit on unrelated topics (see the review on PR #1).

### Task 5: Challenge narrative (after Vishwa's PR)
- Render `requirement.challenge.narrative` (optional string) in the "Challenge result" section of the Decision Card.

### Task 6: Happiness Meter UI (after Arjun's data function)
- Arjun adds `happiness(viewer, vehicle)` to `gate.ts`: per market, share of negative comments covered by
  approved requirements, weighted by sales, `unknown` where there are no comments (China).
- Show it on the vehicle page; it must move when a requirement is approved. Never show `unknown` as 0% or 100%.

### Task 7: Pitch, demo and backup
- Demo script: `PLAN.md` section 6. Slides: problem, our answer, live demo, how scoring works (priority ≠
  confidence), what the AI does vs the PM, data traps we found, scalability (1 / 5 / 7 Series, markets), team.
- Record a backup screen video of the full demo on the live site.
- Before presenting: `npm run db:push` for a clean state, open the live link once (cold start ~4 s),
  set the region to United States.

### Stretch: Portfolio heatmap
- A page comparing topics across the 1, 5 and 7 Series (negative share per topic from `signals`),
  e.g. connectivity and ease of use red on all three.

## 6. You are also the reviewer

Vishwa and Arjun open PRs; you merge them. Check before merging:
- both builds pass locally after `git pull` and `uv run pmw build`;
- schema changes are mirrored in `db.py` and `types.ts` and flagged in the title;
- new `gate.ts` functions are `async`, respect the region, and contain no raw-comment leaks across markets;
- no secrets, no `.env`, no AI attribution in commits;
- the 7 Series demo still works (list, Decision Card, Challenge, region switch, audit).
After merging a schema change, everyone runs `uv run pmw build`; update the live site with `db:push` and deploy.
Ask Vishwa to enable branch protection on `main` (Settings → Branches → require a pull request).

Task 1 from `docs/agent-briefs/GOKUL_AGENT_BRIEF.md`: the structured requirement list BMW asks for (deliverable 2).

## What changed
- **`GET /api/export?vehicle=G70&format=csv|json`** (`web/app/api/export/route.ts`, `web/lib/export.ts`).

  `id`, `title`, `description`, `customer_need`, `root_cause`, `customer_voice`, `findings_and_sources`,

- **Every export is logged** in the audit trail ("exported requirement list", region, format, count).

Requirements carry real comment text in two places: the customer voice and the example quote in each
contradiction ("For example G70-0341: “Customer stated…”"). Both were shown to product managers of other
markets. `gate.ts` now redacts them (`redactComments`) for the Decision Card and the export, e.g.
"Restricted: a comment from United States, visible to that market's product manager."

## Tested
- `uv run pmw build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app components lib`, `npm run build` pass.

This completes the offline evidence-to-decision workflow using all eight supplied BMW files, and adds a validated, cached Anthropic path for a later credentialed run. The user explicitly chose offline-first delivery. Decision forms also handle invalid input, network failure and switching between requirements safely; edited approvals return to review with an audit event.

## Result
- 45 complete core drafts plus 86 equipment-backed candidates integrated from current main; all remain proposed and causal explanations are hypotheses.
- 260 additional comments provisionally classified with `label_source=rule`, while preserving every BMW label; 920 ambiguous comments remain unlabelled. No offline output is presented as live AI.
- Static themes deduplicate comment IDs, union survey mappings, retain equipment matches across member topics and preserve photo lookup. Stable IDs survive rank changes, and prompt samples include minority markets/sources.
- Priority and confidence remain deterministic. G70 core split: **6 act / 2 validate / 3 monitor / 4 park** (baseline before theme merging: 9 / 0 / 2 / 4). With equipment candidates: **8 / 5 / 4 / 21**.
- Build-time Challenge explanations and weight sensitivity appear on the card. China cannot receive US raw quotes through visible content or serialized list props.

## Shared JSON contract ? Gokul and Arjun review
`pipeline/pmw/db.py` documentation and `web/lib/types.ts` add optional challenge `narrative`, `narrative_source`, and `priority_sensitivity`; label provenance adds `rule`. No columns are removed or renamed. `generated_by` distinguishes reviewed templates, live models and cache replay. The UI render is included. Priority stays at 55, preserving MoSCoW; confidence moves to 58 with the reference-case rationale alongside the formula. Equipment matching uses every member topic and retains main's async libSQL/Turso path. No hosted database was replaced or deployment performed.

## Two G70 examples

**Connected services and phone integration**

Before: **Easy-to-use personal eSIM**; root cause: empty. Requirement: The successor 7 Series resolves what customers report about personal eSIM: not user-friendly is the most common complaint. (Template draft. Run the AI step to write the final requirement.)

After: **Connected features that recover gracefully**. Root cause: Working hypothesis: setup and recovery guidance may not match the steps owners expect. The labelled comments (G70-3560, G70-2613) motivate this investigation. Requirement: The successor vehicle shall show connection and activation status and guide owners through recovery when a connected feature becomes unavailable. Owners shall be able to identify the failed connection and restore the affected feature without resetting unrelated preferences.

**Climate control**

Before: **Better climate control**; root cause: empty. Requirement: The successor 7 Series resolves what customers report about climate control: effect, power not ok is the most common complaint. (Template draft. Run the AI step to write the final requirement.)

After: **Comfortable cabin with understandable climate controls**. Root cause: Working hypothesis: control discoverability and perceived cooling performance may contribute to dissatisfaction. The labelled comments (G70-3783, G70-2819) motivate this investigation. Requirement: The successor vehicle shall make airflow and temperature adjustments discoverable and show whether the requested climate setting is active. Passengers shall be able to adjust their settings and verify the result during warm and cold cabin trials.

I reviewed and **merged PR #2** ("Complete offline decision workflow and extend challenge JSON schema", Vishwa's AI tasks) into `main`. The merge is recorded as yours. (That notification was my test server shutting down.)

**What I checked:**

| Region privacy | ✅ China sees 0 US quotes and can't open or approve US-only requirements |
| Secrets, database files, AI attribution | ✅ none |
| Merge conflicts with main | ✅ none |

**What it brings:**
- Every requirement now has a **real root cause, customer need and requirement text**, e.g. "Connected features that recover gracefully". They're written as reviewed templates, because Vishwa had no API key. Each is honestly labelled "needs validation", and root causes are framed as hypotheses.
- **260 more comments labelled.**
- **Topics merged into themes.**
- **The 7 Series spreads across all four quadrants:** 6 Act / 2 Validate / 3 Monitor / 4 Park among the core requirements.
- **The Challenge shows a narrative paragraph and a priority sensitivity range.**

**Things to know:**
- **Requirement IDs changed** to stable hashes (e.g. `R-G70-73240d3417`), so they stay the same when rankings change. Old IDs like `R-G70-001` no longer exist.
- **Your PR #3 now has a conflict** in `web/lib/gate.ts`. Vishwa fixed the same quote leak in his own way, so the two versions overlap. It needs a quick rebase onto his version before it can merge.
- **The live site still runs the old version.** It needs `npm run db:push` plus `vercel deploy --prod` to show Vishwa's work.
- Arjun's quick-win noise (ventilated seats under Drivetrain and so on) is still there until his fix lands.

I can rebase PR #3 onto the new `main` and update the live site next. Want me to?
Why should we rebase PR3. Explain to me in simple terms

Here's the simple version.

**What happened:**
- You and Vishwa both started from the same version of the code.
- You wrote the export feature (PR #3). Vishwa wrote his AI work (PR #2).
- **You both edited the same few lines** in one file, `gate.ts`, the part that hides other markets' customer quotes. You each fixed that leak, in slightly different ways.
- His PR got merged first. Now `main` has his version of those lines, and your PR still has yours.

**Why GitHub won't merge PR #3 now:**
When two people change the *same lines* differently, Git can't guess which version is right, so it stops and asks a human. That's a **conflict**. GitHub won't merge until someone resolves it.

**What "rebase" means:**
It's like saying: "take my changes and replay them **on top of the newest `main`**, as if I'd started from Vishwa's version."

Think of a shared document:
1. You both copied the document this morning.
2. Vishwa rewrote paragraph 3 and handed his copy in first.
3. You also rewrote paragraph 3, plus added a new chapter (the export).
4. Rebasing = taking Vishwa's new document, adding your new chapter to it, and deciding how paragraph 3 should read with both your ideas in it.

**What I'd actually do in this case:**
- **Keep Vishwa's leak fix**, because it's already merged and tested by his 14 browser tests.
- **Keep your export feature**, which is new and doesn't clash with anything.
- Make sure the export uses his privacy rules, so customer quotes still can't leak into another market's download.
- Rerun all the checks, then update PR #3.

**Why not skip it:**
- Without it, PR #3 can't be merged at all.
- If someone forced it through by hand, one of the two leak fixes would get overwritten, and the protection could quietly break.

It's about 10 minutes of work. Want me to do it?

content.text:
**Why it happens:** each requirement in the list is a link to a new address (`…/vehicles/G70?req=R-G70-…`), so clicking one is a full page navigation, not just a panel swap. Next.js has a scroll rule for this: it keeps your scroll position only if the top of the page is still on screen. Once you've scrolled past the car photo banner, Next.js decides you're looking at a "new page" and **jumps back to the top**. So it happens with any requirement once you've scrolled down, not just Must haves.

**The fix is small:**
1. Tell those links not to scroll (`scroll={false}`). This applies to the requirement list and the Act / Validate / Monitor / Park filter chips.
2. One catch: if you click a requirement far down the list, the new detail card might sit above your screen. So add a small helper that brings the **top of the Decision Card** into view, just below the sticky tab bar, rather than the top of the page.

Result: you stay where you are, and the requirement you clicked appears right next to the list.

It's about 15 minutes in your files (`app/vehicles/[code]/page.tsx` and a small client component). Should I fix it on a branch and open a PR?

input.prompt:
You are implementing one task for a hackathon web app called PMW, acting for the repo owner Gokul (frontend lead). You are in an isolated git worktree of the repo (your current working directory). The canonical repo is https://github.com/Vishwa-Balasubramanian/PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels- and `main` is at commit 4ef88d2 or later.

## Read first
- `docs/agent-briefs/phase-2/GOKUL.md` (your brief; you are doing task **G2**), `PLAN.md`, `README.md`.
- Key files: `web/components/DecisionCard.tsx`, `web/app/vehicles/[code]/page.tsx`, `web/lib/gate.ts`, `web/lib/types.ts`, `web/components/ui.tsx`, `web/app/globals.css`.

## Setup (in your worktree)
```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -b gokul/quick-wins origin/main
cd pipeline && uv sync --extra llm && uv run pmw build && cd ..
cd web && npm install && npx next typegen
npx next dev -p 3201    # run in background; use ONLY port 3201
```
The pipeline writes `db/pmw.sqlite` inside your worktree; the web app reads it locally. There is no `.env.local` in your worktree: that is intended. NEVER run `npm run db:push`, never set PMW_USE_REMOTE=1, never deploy, never touch ports 3000/3001.

## Task G2: "You already sell this" banner + Quick wins filter
Data already exists: `requirement.kind` is `"signal" | "quick_win" | "market_conflict"`, and `requirement.already_exists` is `EquipmentMatch[]` with fields `match_type` (`option_same_vehicle | package_same_vehicle | standard_other_vehicle | standard_but_failing`), `feature`, `equipment_name`, `code`, `price_eur`, `source_vehicle`, `feedback_ids` (comment IDs), `note`. Inspect real rows with `sqlite3 db/pmw.sqlite "SELECT id,title,kind,already_exists FROM requirements WHERE kind='quick_win'"` (10 quick wins exist, e.g. the 5 Series "Offer ventilated front seats outside €2,750 Comfort Paket (7VB)").

1. **Banner** (new component `web/components/AlreadySellBanner.tsx`, placed in `DecisionCard.tsx` right under the photo header block / meta line, above the decision buttons): shown when `already_exists` is non-empty. Headline "You already sell this" (or "Standard, but customers report problems" for standard_but_failing). One line per match with wording per match_type: option on this car (name, code, price) · inside a package on this car (package name, code, price) · standard on another BMW (equipment name and source vehicle, e.g. "standard on the 7 Series"; map G70→7 Series, G60→5 Series, F70→1 Series) · standard on this car but customers report problems. Show the price list source ("German price list, July 2026") and that other markets are an assumption. Brand: BMW blue accents, square corners, thin borders, uppercase bold label; the existing tokens are in globals.css (bg-monitor-soft, text-blue, border-line, etc.).
2. **Region privacy for comment IDs**: the banner lists supporting comment IDs, but only those from markets the viewer may see. Do the filtering server-side in `web/lib/gate.ts` inside `getRequirement` (look up the markets of the IDs in `feedback`; keep IDs whose market is in `viewer.markets`; record how many were hidden, e.g. add an optional `hidden_count` per match or a separate field) so no restricted IDs reach client props. Head of product (region ALL) sees all. Also apply the same filtering to `listRequirements` results if `already_exists` is passed to client components there (check whether it is).
3. **Quick wins filter** in the requirement list (vehicle page, the chips row with All / Act / Validate first / Monitor / Park): add a "Quick wins N" chip that filters `kind === 'quick_win'` via a URL param (e.g. `?q=quick`), keeping `scroll={false}` like the other chips. In list rows, quick wins get a small "Quick win" chip next to the quadrant badge.
4. Keep everything responsive at 375px.

## Rules
- Next.js 16 with `cacheComponents: false`; pages use `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`; `params`/`searchParams` are promises. Read `web/node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using unfamiliar APIs. Do NOT use next/font/google. No third-party scripts, fonts or images.
- All DB reads only through async functions in `web/lib/gate.ts`. No SQL in pages/components.
- No schema changes are needed; if you think one is, stop and explain instead.
- Commit messages: plain, descriptive, NO mention of Claude/AI tools, NO "Co-Authored-By" or "Generated with" lines. Same for the PR body.
- Never push to main, never merge.

## Verify (all must pass)
`cd pipeline && uv run pmw build && uv run pmw verify && uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests`; `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint app components lib && npm run build && PMW_USE_REMOTE=0 npm run test:e2e`.
Also check in a browser (you may use the `agent-browser` CLI; set `export AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=g2-quickwins` first; run `agent-browser skills get core` to learn it) or with curl + region cookie `pmw_region` (US, EU, CN, ROW, ALL): the 5 Series ventilated-seats quick win shows the banner with 7VB €2,750; US sees only US comment IDs; CN sees no US IDs; the Quick wins chip lists all quick wins for that car; no horizontal overflow at 375px.

## Deliver
Commit on `gokul/quick-wins`, `git push -u origin gokul/quick-wins`, then open a PR:
`gh pr create -R Vishwa-Balasubramanian/PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels- --base main --head gokul/quick-wins --title "..." --body-file <file>`. The PR body: what changed, how tested (with numbers), privacy handling, no schema change. Do NOT merge.

Final reply to me: the PR URL, a short summary of changes and files touched, test results, and anything you were unsure about.

- `docs/agent-briefs/phase-2/GOKUL.md` (your brief; you are doing task **G3**), `PLAN.md`, `README.md`.
- Key files: `pipeline/pmw/score.py` (the priority formula, weights, thresholds; it may differ from what the brief says, the code is the truth), `pipeline/pmw/cli.py`, `web/lib/gate.ts` (`getWeights`, `listRequirements`, `toRequirement`, `getRequirement`, `exportBundle`), `web/lib/actions.ts`, `web/app/vehicles/[code]/page.tsx`, `web/components/ui.tsx`, `web/lib/moscow.ts`, `web/lib/types.ts`.

## Setup (in your worktree)
```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -b gokul/priority-weights origin/main
cd pipeline && uv sync --extra llm && uv run pmw build && cd ..
cd web && npm install && npx next typegen
npx next dev -p 3202    # run in background; use ONLY port 3202
```
The pipeline writes `db/pmw.sqlite` inside your worktree; the web app reads it locally. There is no `.env.local` in your worktree: intended. NEVER run `npm run db:push`, never set PMW_USE_REMOTE=1, never deploy, never touch ports 3000/3001.

## Task G3: Priority weights sliders + strategy presets
Each requirement stores `priority_factors` (JSON `{factor: {value 0..1, weight, note}}`), `priority`, `confidence`, `quadrant`. The `settings` table holds `weights` (priority weights, confidence weights, thresholds) and `factor_labels`.

1. **`web/lib/score.ts`**: reproduce the pipeline's priority formula exactly (read `score.py`; it is likely `round(100 * Σ weight·value / Σ weight)` but check for any extra terms such as successor scoring or caps). Also the quadrant rule (priority vs. confidence thresholds from settings). Write a test proving that with the default weights the recomputed priority and quadrant equal the stored values for ALL requirements in the database (a Node test in `web/scripts/` run with `node`, or extend the Playwright suite).
2. **Active weights**: persist in the `settings` table under key `weights_active` (JSON: priority weights, preset name or "custom", changed_by, region, changed_at). No new table or column needed (settings is key/value). Add `getActiveWeights()` in `gate.ts`. When active weights exist, every read that exposes priority/quadrant (listRequirements, getRequirement, exportBundle, matrix, home counts — they mostly go through `listRequirements`/`toRequirement`) recomputes priority and quadrant from `priority_factors` with the active weights; confidence stays as stored (challenge may have lowered it). Lists sort by the recomputed priority. MoSCoW groups follow automatically from priority.
3. **Action + audit**: in `web/lib/actions.ts` add an action to set weights (validate: five known factors, numbers 0..1 or percentages, not all zero; reason text required) and one to reset to defaults. Write the settings row and an audit event in the same `writeBatch`: `entity_type = 'weights'`, `entity_id` = 'priority', `field` = 'weights', before/after JSON, rationale = reason, actor = viewer.actor, region. Add a route `web/app/api/weights/route.ts` (POST {action: 'set'|'reset', weights?, preset?, rationale}). Weights are global for the team; any region may change them, and every change is logged with who/region/why.
4. **UI** on the vehicle page above the requirement list: a collapsible "Priority weights" panel (client component, e.g. `web/components/WeightsPanel.tsx`) with five sliders labelled from `factor_labels`, preset buttons (Customer first, Premium experience, Quick wins, China focus, Europe focus — define sensible weight sets in one place and document the idea of each in a comment; "China focus"/"Europe focus" may boost the market factor), a live preview listing how the top 5 would re-order (computed client-side from the requirements' factors passed as props — pass only factor values/ids/titles, nothing else), a required reason field, Apply and Reset buttons. After Apply, `router.refresh()` so the real list re-ranks. Above the list show "Ranking: <preset> · changed by <actor> at <time>" when active weights exist. BMW style: square corners, uppercase bold labels, blue primary button; works at 375px.
5. Update the README section about priority display with one paragraph on weights and presets.

## Rules
- Next.js 16 with `cacheComponents: false`; pages use `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`; `params`/`searchParams` are promises; route handlers use `RouteContext<...>` where params exist. Read `web/node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using unfamiliar APIs. Do NOT use next/font/google. No third-party requests.
- All DB reads through async functions in `web/lib/gate.ts`; writes through `web/lib/actions.ts` with audit events in the same batch.
- Region privacy must stay intact (do not pass raw comment text into new client props).
- No schema changes (settings is key/value). If you believe one is needed, stop and explain.
- Commit messages: plain, descriptive, NO mention of Claude/AI tools, NO "Co-Authored-By" or "Generated with" lines. Same for the PR body.
- Never push to main, never merge.

## Verify (all must pass)
`cd pipeline && uv run pmw build && uv run pmw verify && uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests`; `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint app components lib && npm run build && PMW_USE_REMOTE=0 npm run test:e2e`; plus your formula-equality test.
Browser/curl checks (region cookie `pmw_region`): applying "Customer first" on the 7 Series re-orders the list; the change appears in `/audit` with reason; reload keeps it; Reset restores the original order and priorities exactly; export CSV reflects active weights; no horizontal overflow at 375px. You may use the `agent-browser` CLI (set `export AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=g3-weights`; run `agent-browser skills get core` first).
Leave the database in default state at the end (Reset) — not essential since it is your worktree copy.

## Deliver
Commit on `gokul/priority-weights`, `git push -u origin gokul/priority-weights`, open a PR with `gh pr create -R Vishwa-Balasubramanian/PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels- --base main --head gokul/priority-weights --title "..." --body-file <file>`. PR body: what changed, the formula and presets, how tested (numbers), audit behaviour, no schema change. Do NOT merge.

Final reply to me: the PR URL, a short summary, files touched, test results, and anything you were unsure about (especially any difference between score.py and the brief).
